From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Argentum Health — Renewal uplift proposal / throughput & SLA

Hi Nuria —

Following our Q2 usage run-rate and the renewal window in November, I put together a short proposal to upgrade Argentum to Redwood Premium SLA and reserve dedicated capacity for your model workloads. High level:

- Dedicated capacity pool sized for steady 120 QPS (burst to 350 QPS) for inference workloads tied to Core API.
- Latency SLOs under Premium: 95th <= 120ms; 99th <= 350ms (region: us-west).
- Annual commit pricing with an on-demand burst bucket; we can structure a 12 or 24 month term.

I've attached a one-page proposal and a throughput model so you can see the cost/benefit math. If you like, we can run a short pre-renewal pilot that simulates your September traffic to validate tail latency and cost.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm whether Argentum wants a 12 vs 24 month commit.
2) If yes, we'll route to procurement and send a redline-friendly term sheet + DocuSign.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical sync (SE + SRE) to lock down capacity assumptions.

Thanks — available tomorrow afternoon if that works.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas —

Appreciate the overview. A few clarifying questions before we loop procurement in formally:

- Can you confirm the SLA targets at our current cardinality? We have variable sequence lengths; how do you measure the 95th/99th? Is that end-to-end API time including auth and network hop?
- We currently have a hard cost ceiling for FY29. Can you give the delta vs our current committed plan (I can share our current invoice if helpful).
- Procurement will need a hard burst definition and failure fallback policy (what happens if Dedicated pool is saturated?).

We are interested in a pilot but will need clear acceptance criteria: latency, error-rate, and a weekly check-in cadence. Also send the redlineable version of the T&Cs when ready.

Subject: Argentum Health — Premium SLA offer, pilot plan and next steps

Hi Nuria / team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal review, here's a concise offer designed to map to procurement's asks and provide clear pilot acceptance criteria. Attached: redwood_premium_sla_terms_2028.docx (redline-friendly) and an updated throughput workbook.

Offer summary:
- Premium SLA (12-month commit example shown):
  • Dedicated capacity: steady 120 QPS, burst capacity to 350 QPS for short windows (defined as any 1-minute window).
  • Latency SLOs (measured at Redwood ingress): 95th <= 120ms, 99th <= 300ms.
  • Availability SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for dedicated pool.
  • Failure fallback: automatic spillover to compatible multi-tenant model variant with per-token throttling; Redwood will maintain an on-call escalation channel and crediting for SLA misses.
- Pricing (example):
  • 12mo commit: $280k/year (includes access to Premium support and 24/7 on-call during pilot).
  • 24mo commit: $520k/2yrs (5% discount applied).
  • Burst bucket add-on: $30k/year buys 3M burst tokens; additional burst priced at on-demand rates.

Pilot definition (4 weeks):
- Scope: mirror production traffic for Core API at 75–100% of typical daily traffic for two weeks, then full traffic surge window (simulate a product launch day).
- Acceptance: 95th <= 140ms and 99th <= 350ms during the two full-traffic days; error rate < 0.2% sustained. Weekly syncs with Evelyn, daily slack channel with SEs.
- Deliverables: weekly dashboard, incident runbook, signed term-sheet to move to committed capacity.

Next steps:
1) If you agree, I'll send the redlineable DocuSign envelope and route to procurement.
2) We can kick off a technical pre-check next Tuesday with Marissa and Rishi to validate input traffic sampling.

Attaching: redwood_premium_sla_terms_2028.docx, throughput_model_argentum_v2.xlsx

Open to adjusting SLOs if Argentum needs a different tail target; we balanced cost vs SLA for the numbers above.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Thanks for the detail and for pulling the pilot acceptance into the terms. Procurement reviewed the pricing buckets and prefers the 12-month commit with the burst add-on option. They also asked for the following in the redline:

- Explicit monthly reporting cadence and a named point of contact for incident escalations.
- A clause that preserves our right to invoke a temporary capacity increase (30% for up to 7 days) once per quarter without penalty.
- PO intent attached; procurement will issue a formal PO after final redlines.

We're happy to proceed with the pilot and will get procurement's PO over once we see the DocuSign with the requested clauses. Please include procurement@argentumhealth.com on the envelope.

Appreciate the responsiveness — please loop legal on both sides for redlines.

Best,
